_note: v2.4 plan 03 live gate 2. Real model, real extraction at cadence 1, so-scenario --sandbox --group 'Group: Arin, DM Narrator', lanes only. Each case makes a boundary with a /sendas reply (no main-model call) and acts while that boundary's cadence read request is in flight (an attempt whose read already answered is recorded as raced and retried). CONTROL: a player line appended AFTER the read's window does not abort it: the request completes, its audit lands, no lapse is journaled. NOOP: the player line INSIDE the in-flight window is edited (st-actions' edit path: text, updateMessageBlock, saveChat, MESSAGE_EDITED) with no transition fired, so the rollback restores nothing: the request must reject as AbortError, the journal gains the lapse (no error, no breaker); the run then records whether any later read covers the edited message. APPLIED: pay_discussed and go (a code quality no read can set) are set through setQuality (what /cp set calls; an in-page /cp answers only in Author view since v2.6 T3-4, 01a11e07) so the next boundary fires hall->yard, and while the NEXT boundary's cadence read is in flight, the line consumed by the fired boundary is edited: the read is aborted (the edit is at or before its window end), the rollback applies and its P0 re-read (reason rollback:*) covers the edited message. The APPLIED case must not also produce a reread:lapsed audit: the lapsed read merges into the rollback's P0 re-read (one read, not two). LAST STEP: the noop case must have been re-read for the edit by the scheduler's lapse re-read (exactly one reread:lapsed audit covering the edited message, landed before the next turn, v2.4 plan 03 live-found fix D2); it fails with DEFECT otherwise, and names any read that covered it only incidentally (a stall reconcile). Measured: abort latency (MESSAGE_EDITED emit -> fetch rejection), llama-server requests_processing (/metrics) before the read, before the edit and for 5 s after (the backend is shared with the other lane and the main session, so this is context, not proof), the follow-up read's queue wait = wall time minus llama's prompt_ms + predicted_ms.
